agents.reasoning: Round 2. Facts: Q2-26 revenue $1.924B (+53%), adj. EBITDA $1.614B (84%), 335.3M shares, net debt about $0.46B, Q3 guide $2.055-2.085B. FY26/FY27 consensus EPS is $15.67/$20.00, with FY27 down from $21.16 over 60 days. At $281 the stock is at about 14x FY27 EPS and about a 6% FCF yield, so the drawdown is de-rating rather than an earnings collapse. The supervisor's corrections, which I checked: (1) the SEC inquiry is closed. AdTechRadar (Aug 5 2026) reports the CFO said on the Q2 call it closed with no recommended enforcement action. Bloomberg had reported it 'still active' as late as Feb 20 2026, so my round-1 premise was stale, not invented, but it was wrong as of October. I removed it from the bear story and catalysts and cut the bear probability from 30% to 27%. (2) Edgewater's Q4 +8-9% q/q is only about 1-2% below consensus, so I cut my EPS haircut from 7.5% to 4.5%, keeping part for Wells Fargo's Sep 30 traffic-weighted pixel data, which I confirmed across Yahoo/Stocktwits and Investing.com. (3) I dropped the thin Polymarket recession market (about $9.7K volume). Base rates: Mauboussin and Callahan (Counterpoint Global, May 2025) find a median peak-to-trough drawdown of 85% across 6,500 stocks from 1985 to 2024, and more than half never regain their prior high. I tried the primary PDF again and Morgan Stanley returned 403, so the figures come from the study's own landing page and search abstract. That keeps a return to $700+ in 12 months a tail outcome (about 5%). The TTD analog (a second straight year down about 67%) argues for persistence while revisions stay negative; Meta 2023 and APP 2023 argue for violent rebounds once they turn. Valuation: P/E $333, FCF yield $330, EV/EBITDA $292, blended 40/35/25 to $322 (round 1: $315). Scenarios $175/$310/$475 at 27/46/27% (mean about $318). The ladder is a 50/50 blend of that scenario mixture (inner sigmas 0.28-0.35) and a single lognormal (median $296, sigma 0.60). The result is P(>=$281) of 0.55 and a median of about $300, nudged up 1-2 points from round 1. I disagree with no supervisor finding. My fair value ($322) lands near its $320 independently: my FCF leg is higher and my EV/EBITDA leg lower. The thesis break moves to $185. Limits: no option data was used; the Morgan Stanley PDF was blocked; there are no APP-specific prediction markets.
